newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian call stays firm, ends at 6.0-6.50 percent.
newsitem.headline: Indian call stays firm, ends at 6.0-6.50 percent.

text.p: Indian call rates closed firm at 6.0-6.5 percent on Monday after opening at 5.5-6.25 percent, dealers said.
"Demand wasn't that much, considering the new fortnight has just begun, but the sentiment was firm," said a dealer.
Dealers attributed the sentiment to three auctions last week -- 91-day treasury bill, 364-day treasury bill and 14-day treasury bill -- soaking up considerable liquidity.
The tax outflow in mid-June are expected to take up close to 20.0 billion rupees, dealers said.
Monday's subscription at the repo auction at 48 billion rupees was higher than expected and would mean call rates continuing firm on Tuesday, they said.
The securities market was subdued on Monday thanks largely to the firm call market, dealers said.
The 12.14 percent security maturing in 2000 was active, posting a handsome rise in price, they said.
